      "text": "Interrupted in-place writes could corrupt data files without atomic updates or checksum detection",
      "quote": "How worried are we about file corruption here? I thought the main reason we use leveldb and sqlite databases in places like this where we don't need indexing is that they support atomic updates, so yo",

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Race between writer creating log_flag.dat and calling ApplyLog allows another process to apply the WAL first, causing the writer to throw an error",

      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author gated lock file flushing behind read-only flag and introduced OpenMode",

      ],
      "other_replies": [],

      "status_by_id": "c:4791777117",
      "status_by_quote": "Gated lock file flushing behind a read-only flag to avoid the cross-process log file contention issues flagged by @willcl-ark."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4827817824",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Add a separate directory lock for writers only that fails fast on a second writer process instead of busy-waiting",

      "status_by_id": "c:4833928218",
      "status_by_quote": "Also introduced a write directory lock that gets taken on instantiation and yielded on destruction."
    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Whether not exposing BlockTreeStore::OpenMode::READ in btck_chainstate_manager_create is intentional, and if wiring it through the kernel API is planned as a follow-up",

      "status_note": "author confirmed intentional and suggested a separate discussion",

    },

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",

claims.text: Race between writer creating log_flag.dat and calling ApplyLog allows another process to apply the WAL first, causing the writer to throw an error

claims.status_by_quote: Gated lock file flushing behind a read-only flag to avoid the cross-process log file contention issues flagged by @willcl-ark.

claims.text: Add a separate directory lock for writers only that fails fast on a second writer process instead of busy-waiting
claims.quote: add a separate directory lock for writers only, one that's taken for the whole lifetime of the store (in WRITE/WIPE mode) and fails fast on a second writer process instead of busy-waiting
claims.status_note: author added write directory lock and functional test
claims.status_by_quote: Also introduced a write directory lock that gets taken on instantiation and yielded on destruction.

claims.quote: This is a no-op on Windows. I think this can lead to several edge case issues, like the block tree being marked as unpruned when blocks have already been removed, or the WAL not being applied atomical
